summary: Shoppers size the battery first (about 300 Wh for electronics, 1 kWh as the default, 2 kWh and up for a refrigerator through an outage), then check that continuous watts cover the largest appliance, then trade price against weight and whether the unit can take an extra battery. In the last 60 days EcoFlow shipped the DELTA 3000/3800 Gen4 and RIVER Gen4, and BLUETTI added the Elite 100 mini; Black Friday pricing has pushed tested 1 kWh stations to $360-$470 and a 3 kWh station to $899. Growatt's HELIOS 3600 went the other way, from $1,399 to $1,599, and several BLUETTI stations are pre-orders shipping December to February.

axes.why: OutdoorGearLab gives 60% of its score to power output and measures delivered energy for each unit; ChatGPT sized the battery in 6 of 6 chats (project brief) and split picks at about 290 Wh, 1 kWh and 2 kWh. GearJunkie sets its price tiers by capacity (300-600 Wh budget, 1,000-2,000 Wh mid-tier).

breakpoints.why: TSA: spare lithium batteries go in carry-on only; 'with airline approval, passengers may also carry up to two spare larger lithium ion batteries (101-160 Wh)'. A station above 160 Wh cannot fly (read 2026-11-27).

Phones-and-laptop class. OutdoorGearLab measured 260 Wh from the Jackery Explorer 300 and says a station this size suits blackouts of under an hour; GearJunkie's budget tier starts at 300 Wh (read 2026-11-27).
The default class. OutdoorGearLab measured 870-910 Wh from five stations rated 1,024-1,070 Wh, so a 1 kWh station delivers under 0.9 kWh (read 2026-11-27).
OutdoorGearLab: for electric camping 'you'll want at least a 2,000 Wh power station, and one with at least 2,000 AC watt support'. ChatGPT moved refrigerator-outage shoppers to 2 kWh (project brief).

Home-backup class. GearJunkie's Best Home Backup pick is 3,072 Wh and ran a full-size fridge and a chest freezer together over 24-hour runs; EcoFlow's new DELTA 3000 Gen4 is the same size (read 2026-11-27).
The 5 kWh class is where single units carry 240 V and 7,200 W: Jackery's Explorer 5000 Plus page gives 7,200 W rated and both 120 V and 240 V (read 2026-11-27).

axes.label: Continuous AC output: the biggest appliance it can run
axes.why: GearJunkie weights power output most heavily (30%) and tells buyers to 'aim for at least a 2,000 W continuous inverter' and to buy an inverter '25% to 50% larger than the highest capacity appliance'. ChatGPT split picks at 300, 600, 1,500, 1,800, 2,000, 2,400 and 2,600 W (project brief).

breakpoints.why: Electronics only. GearJunkie's 300 W Jackery Explorer 300 tripped its protection in about 10 seconds on an electric fireplace or a skill saw (read 2026-11-27).

The standard US household outlet is NEMA 5-15, 15 A at 125 V; 15 A at 120 V is 1,800 W, so wall-outlet appliances top out here. GearJunkie: '1,800 W is as fast as you can get from a typical 15A wall outlet' (read 2026-11-27).
GearJunkie's stated minimum for most household appliances and power tools: 'at least a 2,000 W continuous inverter' (read 2026-11-27).
NEMA 5-20 is the 20 A household outlet; 20 A at 120 V is 2,400 W, the ceiling for one 20 A receptacle (read 2026-11-27).
NEMA TT-30 is 'a 120 V 30 A recreational vehicle standard'; 30 A at 120 V is 3,600 W, so a station under 3,600 W cannot feed a 30 A RV its full service (read 2026-11-27).

breakpoints.why: The 120 V 30 A RV standard used at RV parks; full service needs 3,600 W behind it.
NEMA 14-30 (dryers, ranges), L14-30 (backup generators) and 14-50 (50 A RV shore power, EV charging) are 250 V connectors; a 120 V-only station cannot feed them.

axes.label: Recharge speed from the wall and from solar

breakpoints.why: Under an hour to full separates the fast 1 kWh stations: OutdoorGearLab timed the Anker C1000 Gen 2 at 0.8 h, the DELTA 3 and DJI Power 1000 V2 at 0.9 h, and the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 at 1.8 h (read 2026-11-27).

axes.why: Makers sell the 10 ms figure as what keeps a NAS or server up: EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Max page says '10ms Auto-Switch: Fast enough to keep critical devices like NAS systems and servers running smoothly'. GearJunkie reports transfer times in its reviews.

breakpoints.why: The figure makers and GearJunkie cite for computers and NAS (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max, EcoFlow US store, read 2026-11-27). Growatt's HELIOS 3600 lists 15 ms; our AC180 record lists 20 ms.

axes.why: GearJunkie: LFP 'can retain their lifespan through 3,000 to 6,000 charge cycles' against 'a lifespan of just 500-ish cycles' for NMC. Bob Vila says LFP has 'nearly twice the expected lifespan'. ChatGPT told a first-time buyer to look for LFP (project brief).

breakpoints.why: The floor GearJunkie gives for LFP; an NMC station sits far below it (read 2026-11-27).

axes.label: Can jump-start a car
axes.why: Google completes 'portable power station with' with 'jump starter' (read 2026-11-27). Few stations have a jump-start port; VTOMAN's cable listing names the ones that do.

breakpoints.why: A '12V jump start port' on the station plus a VTOMAN jumper cable starts a 12 V vehicle (VTOMAN US store, read 2026-11-27).

rules: Capacity means rated watt-hours. Delivered AC energy runs about 85-89% of it (OutdoorGearLab measured 870-910 Wh from five stations rated 1,024-1,070 Wh), and GearJunkie plans on 75%. Output means continuous AC watts: BLUETTI's Power Lifting, EcoFlow's X-Boost and Growatt's Watt+ are modes for resistive loads and are not rated output. Cycle ratings compare only at the same end point (80%, 70% or 60%). A price is the maker's US store price on the day, with the link price beside it when a code was cart-tested. Black Friday prices this week sit far below list, so every figure needs its date. Pre-order status and ship date belong beside the price, since most BLUETTI stations here ship between December and February. Weight comes from a reviewer's scale when one exists (OutdoorGearLab weighs), otherwise from the maker. A TT-30 outlet on a station rated under 3,600 W does not deliver 30 A. 240 V means split-phase from one unit unless stated; 240 V from two paired units is a different answer. Bob Vila's table for the Elite 200 V2 disagrees with its own text, so its figures need the maker's page. OutdoorGearLab lists the Anker C1000 Gen 2 at 1,800 W while Anker rates 2,000 W.

lines.question: which portable power station has a 240V outlet

lines.asked: Google suggestion 'portable power station with 240v output', read 2026-11-27; our /best-240v-portable-power-station drew 6 visits, https://suggestqueries.google.com/complete/search?client=firefox&hl=en&gl=us&q=portable+power+station+with+
